chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Recognize your Imam, for when you have recognized him, it will not harm you whether this matter comes earlier or is delayed.”

key_terms.إِمَامَكَ: your Imam; the divinely appointed guide whose recognition is essential
key_terms.اعْرِفْ: recognize; attain true knowledge and acknowledgment
key_terms.تَأَخَّرَ: is delayed; occurs later than expected
key_terms.تَقَدَّمَ: comes earlier; is brought forward in time
key_terms.لَمْ يَضُرَّكَ: it will not harm you; it will not adversely affect your faith or standing
key_terms.هَذَا الْأَمْرُ: this matter; the divinely ordained affair referenced in the narration

ai.seo_question: Why does recognizing the Imam matter even if the divine affair is delayed?
ai.summary: This hadith emphasizes the central importance of recognizing the Imam. Once a person truly knows his Imam, the timing of this matter—whether advanced or delayed—does not harm him. It highlights maʿrifah of the Imam as a foundational element of faith and steadfastness.
